en: Dr. Fe del Mundo's bamboo incubator uses a water jacket to absorb heat from a lamp, keeping newborns warm without electricity.
When both houses of Congress approve a bill, it goes to the President, whose signature officially turns it into a law.
If the Supreme Court finds a new law violates the Constitution, the justices can declare it invalid to protect citizens' rights.
Filipino scientists burn coconut shells without oxygen to create porous charcoal that traps and removes toxins from drinking water.
When a voter shades the circle next to a candidate's name, the automated machine reads the mark and counts the vote.
Workers strip the stalks of the abaca plant and dry the fibers so weavers can spin them into strong ropes.
Clappers strike the bamboo poles together on the offbeat, forcing dancers to jump quickly to avoid having their ankles caught.
Farmers carve stone walls along mountain slopes to create flat steps that hold rainwater and prevent soil from washing away.
Dr. Angel Alcala discovered that papaya enzymes break down tough meat proteins, making the flesh tender for cooking.
Weavers interlace thin pineapple fibers on a loom to create a breathable fabric that keeps the wearer cool in tropical heat.
Tiny coral polyps secrete calcium carbonate to build hard skeletons, which accumulate over time to form protective coastal reefs.
When the conductor raises the baton, the musicians play the opening notes, signaling citizens to stand and show respect.
